name: emberstead

visual_review.silhouette: Three separate steep-roof cottages, a lower copper-roof well, an open fenced plot and farm. Player house has a forward wing and covered porch, with the tallest capped chimney as a focal point.
visual_review.palette: Dark roofs contrast with pale walls; spruce frames tie buildings together and weathered copper is limited to low porch/wing/well roofs. Ground and farm inflate the whole-scene palette count.
visual_review.depth: Roof overhangs, low stone plinths, porch posts, window boxes and shutters are visible. Main side wall was the longest pale panel; one timber pier was inserted during the single revision.
visual_review.roofline: Steep paired stair slopes and dark capped ridges are visible. Lower copper roof sections distinguish the entrance wing and porches from the main volume.
visual_review.light: Visible warm lanterns mark front porches, farm corners, well and expansion gate; interior lanterns hang below real beams.
visual_review.grounding: Dark raised plinths, moss and shrub details soften the walls. Preview is level for asset review; runtime grades each module independently and creates connecting roads.
visual_review.limits: This is the MCP renderer, not a game screenshot. Crop geometry appears as flat color patches in this renderer. Exterior roads are deliberately excluded from the schematic because runtime generates them on terrain.

style_notes: MCP warns that the entire six-module scene is nearly square. This is a village layout, not a square building; the player house itself has asymmetric projecting volumes.
MCP counts eight materials above five percent across all modules including farm/ground. Residential palette remains spruce, calcite, dark stone, copper accents.
